As a Pilot I will tell you this not exactly the case. We did make a job redundant and it wasn’t the airline pilot, it was the flight engineer. Monitoring of engines and systems, navigation and en-route information was the preview of the flight engineer. Then Flight Management Computers took that job and pilots became the keepers of the instruments. With General Aviation jobs all over the world being in short supply there is less pilot’s able to pass through the pipe line due to lack of hours. This means that airline pilots are in short supply and there is no way to get people experience short of paying for their hours. I can very easily see many domestic flights going one pilot with remote or AI technology. Not good for me personally but drones have replaced a lot of the small jobs that pilots used to have in order to create hours/experience.
